answer: Reputation-weighted message quota: each identity's send allowance follows a rolling average of peer acknowledgments, adjusted by a decay prism that refracts old activity into shrinking influence. A new identity starts near zero and rises only as independent responders answer, so a rising tide of acknowledgments lifts quota slowly for newcomers. When a cluster of fresh identities suddenly boosts each other, the system measures the delta between internal and external reply rates and throttles the whole cluster's allowance to the lower figure.
